rule.entry: Opening-range breakout: price breaks the high or low of the first session bars. Fourteen families were tested, including gap continuation and a VVG reversal.

rule.parameters: Friction floor 2.0 MNQ points. ORB long hold H=15 bars. Stop example 20 points.

performance.quote: ORB Long (H=15) gross +4.82 points, net +2.82, T-Net +0.88, N (OOS) 447 total. Failure mode: T-statistic < 2.0; year-unstable. VVG Classifier Reversal net +13.49, T-Net +1.26, N 35. Gap Continuation Short net +14.52, T-Net +1.46.
performance.location: Table 13 and section 4.1. Abstract: maximum gross return of the families that miss friction is 0.07 to 1.50 points. Section 4.1: 80.7% stop-out rate at a 20-point stop.

papers.after_costs: yes — net of a 2-point round trip

papers.title: A Validated Volatility-Volume-Gap Classifier for Regime Identification in MNQ Intraday Data

rule.entry: Tag the day if first-30-minute return, absolute overnight gap, and first-bar volume deviation are each above the expanding-window 66.7th percentile computed through the prior day.
rule.side: The tag itself is not a side. The traded cousin fades the opening move when a regression of the first 30 minutes on the last 30 minutes predicts reversal.
rule.exit: Fade is judged on the last 30 minutes. A 15:30 close fade was also tried and did not reach 30 trades.
rule.parameters: Pseudocode on the PDF: r1_thresh, gap_thresh, vol_thresh = percentile_66.7 of history through D-1. vol_dev uses a 20-day rolling baseline. classifier[D]=1 only if all three exceed.

performance.quote: Activates on 40/947 days (Table 2, 4.2%). Next-day return +0.295% on tagged days vs +0.039% otherwise, spread +0.256% (25.6 bps), Table 3. Peak reversal by close 97/125 = 77.6%, mean giveback 11.73 points, Table 5. Fade: N=127 OOS, mean net +7.80 pts, T=+1.46, win rate 52.0%, 2024 net -26.75. Marked FAIL.
performance.location: Tables 2, 3, 5 and the OOS metric block (pdftotext page 8).

papers.after_costs: the +7.80 point fade is net; the 25.6 bp next-day spread is a return difference, not an option P&L

papers.title: Expected Stock Returns and Variance Risk Premia
papers.market_and_sample: S&P 500, January 1990 to December 2007, monthly observations.
papers.horizon: 1 to 24 months; strongest at the quarterly horizon

rule.entry: Variance risk premium = model-free implied variance minus realized variance from high-frequency returns. High premium predicts higher future equity returns. For an option buyer the usable filter is the opposite of selling rich vol: do not buy premium when implied variance is far above realized variance.
rule.side: Equity timing is long the index when the premium is high. That is not a long-option trade.
rule.exit: Their regressions are monthly to two-year holding windows, not an intraday flat.
rule.filters: Model-free implied vol, not Black-Scholes IV. Realized variation from intraday data.
rule.parameters: Quarterly regression is the one they call impressive. No India VIX threshold is stated.

data_needed.note: Partial only. Daily India VIX is a proxy; we do not store a full OTM book.

performance.quote: The quarterly return regression results in a much more impressive t-statistic of 2.86 and a corresponding R^2 of 6.82%.
performance.location: Body text and the monthly-horizon variance-premium table (adjusted R^2 row: 1 month 1.07, 3 months 6.82, 6 months 5.42). Also: Beckers and Bouten (2005) 'a market timing strategy based on the ratio of implied to historical volatilities doubles the Sharpe ratio relative to that of a constant S&P 500 exposure.'

papers.after_costs: not a trading P&L; regression R^2
red_flags: horizon is months, so theta kills a long ATM hold
equity timing is the other side of buying options when vol is rich

papers.title: Options Order Flow, Volatility Demand and Variance Risk Premium
papers.market_and_sample: Nifty options, 1 July 2015 to 31 December 2015. Five order-book snapshots a day. Minute Nifty for 5-minute realized variance.
papers.horizon: daily change in the variance premium; realized-variance innovation over the next month

rule.entry: Volatility demand = average of vega-weighted call-plus-put order imbalance at each strike and expiry, across 11:00, 12:00, 13:00, 14:00 and 15:00. Regress the daily change in variance premium on demand by moneyness.
rule.side: No option buy is specified. A positive premium change is said to line up with higher subsequent realized variance, which would be a reason to own vol only if the premium itself is not already rich.
rule.filters: Moneyness log(K/F). They drop the deepest ITM wings because activity is tiny.
rule.parameters: India VIX squared divided by 12 is monthly risk-neutral variance. Realized variance is the sum of 5-minute squared returns over 30 calendar days. GMM, Newey-West lags 7 and 30.

data_needed.note: Near strikes only; not a full chain.
Only from Monday, not a history.
